candidates.attacker_control: Archive entry names are fully attacker-controlled for any format (zip/tar/7z/cpio/etc.). Applications using the public high-level extractor `Expander.expand(...)` (public API since 1.17, ships in the main jar) on untrusted archives supply attacker-chosen names to `new File(targetDirectory, nextEntry.getName())`.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Canonicalization resolves symlinks and `..` for existing path components, so escapes to arbitrary unrelated paths are rejected by the same check (plain `../../outside` fails) - the bypass requires the prefix-sibling condition. Absolute entry names are not an independent bypass because `new File(parent, child)` relativizes an absolute child in this JDK behavior and canonicalization then stays under the target. Directory entries are subject to the same flawed check. I also confirmed the class contains no other sanitization layer (no File.separator, no Path.startsWith, no `..` filtering) and that the only pending 1.18 changelog entry is precisely this path-traversal edge case, which the snapshot code does not yet handle.
candidates.impact: Arbitrary file write outside the intended extraction directory (limited to paths whose canonical string is prefixed by the target path, i.e. the target itself or its string-prefix siblings), including creation of directories via mkdirs and overwriting existing files if permissions allow. In deployments where the target directory is a string prefix of a security-relevant sibling (e.g. `/srv/app/data` vs `/srv/app/data-config`, or a user's `.ss` vs `.ssh`-style layout), this can overwrite configuration or data files. The project itself classified the corresponding fix as a path-traversal fix.
candidates.prerequisites: (1) Application extracts an attacker-supplied archive with Expander; (2) the extraction target has (or an attacker can arrange) a sibling directory whose canonical path is prefixed by the target's canonical path (the exact edge case described in the repo's own changes.xml 1.18 entry, e.g. `/x/out` vs `/x/out-anything`); (3) attacker can guess or enumerate the target path (often fixed/known). Multiple `..` segments and directory entries can be combined.
candidates.root_cause: Expander.expand(ArchiveEntrySupplier, EntryWriter, File) computes `String targetDirPath = targetDirectory.getCanonicalPath()` (Expander.java:241) and validates each entry with `if (!f.getCanonicalPath().startsWith(targetDirPath))` (Expander.java:244-248). A plain String.startsWith on a canonical path does not enforce directory containment: if a sibling directory exists whose canonical path extends the target's canonical path (e.g. target `/data/out`, sibling `/data/out-old`), an entry name such as `../out-old/file` canonicalizes to `/data/out-old/file`, which still startsWith `/data/out`. The check passes and the file is created via `Files.newOutputStream(f.toPath())` (Expander.java:258-259), after `parent.mkdirs()` (Expander.java:254-257). There is no trailing File.separator, no java.nio.file.Path component-wise comparison, and no `..`/name sanitization anywhere in the class.
candidates.title: Path traversal in Expander.expand writes outside target directory via sibling-directory prefix bypass
candidates.trace: nextEntry.getName() (untrusted, e.g. `../out-old/evil.conf`) -> `new File(targetDirectory, nextEntry.getName())` (244) -> `f.getCanonicalPath()` resolves `..` to `/<parent>/out-old/evil.conf` -> `.startsWith("/<parent>/out")` is true -> containment check passes -> `parent.mkdirs()` (255) -> `Files.newOutputStream(f.toPath())` (258) creates/overwrites the file outside the intended directory. A vanilla `../../etc/passwd`-style name is rejected because its canonical string does not share the target prefix; the bypass specifically uses a prefix-sibling path, which matches the pending changelog entry (src/changes/changes.xml:47-52).
candidates.unverified: No runtime reproduction or test execution (not permitted). Exploitability depends on the deployment: Expander is an examples/high-level helper, not the core streams; the sibling-directory condition must be satisfiable, and write success depends on filesystem permissions. I could not consult upstream history/patches to confirm exactly how the fix was implemented, so the claim that this snapshot is the reverted-fix state (rather than merely pre-fix) is an inference from the presence of the 2018-06-15 changes.xml entry combined with the still-vulnerable check.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-22 Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal'); root-cause CWE-697 incorrect comparison / CWE-20

coverage_summary: All 264 model-visible files were in scope (source_root_files=264; P1 index indexed 264/264, 0 missing, complete; no binary/sensitive/symlink exclusions). There are no test files in the snapshot and tests were not run. I read in depth: Expander (candidate), ZipArchiveInputStream (all 1214 lines), ZipFile central-directory/local-header paths, ExtraFieldUtils, AsiExtraField, X0017, SevenZFile (headers/FilesInfo/NID parsing, AES decoder), TarUtils and TarArchiveInputStream parsing, CpioArchiveInputStream, ArjArchiveInputStream, DumpArchiveInputStream/TapeInputStream, LZWInputStream/UnshrinkingInputStream, ExplodingInputStream, Deflate64 HuffmanDecoder/Deflate64CompressorInputStream, BZip2CompressorInputStream, BitInputStream, IOUtils, BoundedInputStream (both variants). I skimmed rather than line-audited: ZipArchiveOutputStream, TarArchiveOutputStream, Cpio/Ar/Arj output streams, BZip2CompressorOutputStream/BlockSort, LZ4/Snappy/Brotli/Zstd/XZ/Pack200 wrapper code, ArchiveStreamFactory/CompressorStreamFactory, ChangeSetPerformer/ChangeSet, ParallelScatterZipCreator/ScatterZipOutputStream, and site XML.
limitations: No code execution, tests, fuzzing, or runtime confirmation; findings are source-level leads only.
No upstream diff, patch, CVE/CWE label, or external advisory was consulted (prohibited), so the mapping between this snapshot and a specific historical fix/CVE is inferred, not verified.
The P1 relation index supplies only syntactic/navigation candidates and does not prove reachability, data flow, or exploitability; every cited edge was re-checked against source text.
The snapshot has no test directory, so test resources that might exercise the vulnerable paths were unavailable.
The Expander candidate's real-world impact depends on deployment-specific directory layouts (sibling-prefix condition) and whether applications use the examples-package API for untrusted archives.
Sections listed as skimmed in the coverage summary may contain additional defects not surfaced by this review.

rejected_leads.lead: Infinite loop in ZipArchiveInputStream.read / readStored / readStoredEntry (CVE-2018-11771 candidate, version window 1.18-SNAPSHOT fits)
rejected_leads.reason: Extensive source audit of read(), readStored(), readStoredEntry(), bufferContainsSignature(), cacheBytesRead(), closeEntry(), skip(), readDeflated/readFromInflater found explicit anti-loop/EOF guards (r <= 0 -> IOException('Truncated ZIP file'), lastStoredEntry ByteArrayInputStream returning -1 at exhaustion, inf.finished() -> -1, in.read()==-1 -> -1). I could not identify a concrete crafted-input path that makes read() return 0 persistently, so source evidence is insufficient for a candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: AsiExtraField.parseFromLocalFileData `new byte[length - WORD]` and X0017_StrongEncryptionHeader.parseFileFormat/parseCentralDirectoryFormat unchecked sizes
rejected_leads.reason: Crafted short extra fields can cause NegativeArraySizeException/AIOOBE (DoS via uncaught RuntimeException), but these code shapes exist in upstream versions of the file and the impact is exception-based, not memory corruption; no loop or write primitive established.

rejected_leads.lead: SevenZFile AES256SHA256Decoder KDF loop `for (long j = 0; j < (1L << numCyclesPower); j++)` with attacker-controlled numCyclesPower up to 62
rejected_leads.reason: Plausible CPU-exhaustion DoS (effectively unbounded SHA-256 iterations), but I could not verify absence of an upstream bound in this snapshot's call path, and it is a different root cause than the primary candidate; left unconfirmed.

rejected_leads.lead: SevenZFile.readFilesInfo `while (true)` property loop and ArjArchiveInputStream.readHeader magic rescan loop as infinite loops
rejected_leads.reason: Both consume input every iteration and terminate via EOFException/BufferUnderflowException at end of input; no zero-progress path found in source.
Negative array size -> uncaught exception (DoS-by-exception) only; low impact and no craftable infinite loop.

summary: Reviewed the full 264-file Apache Commons Compress 1.18-SNAPSHOT tree (pom.xml version 27, changes.xml 1.18 section open, only 2018-06-15 entry). Audit focused on attacker-controlled parsing paths: zip (ZipArchiveInputStream, ZipFile, ExtraFieldUtils/AsiExtraField/X0017), tar, cpio, arj, dump/TapeInputStream, 7z (SevenZFile, AES256SHA256Decoder), codecs (LZW/Unshrinking/Exploding, Deflate64/HuffmanDecoder, BZip2, LZ4, snappy), and utils (IOUtils, BoundedInputStream, BitInputStream). The strongest, source-evidenced issue is a path traversal in the public high-level extractor `org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.examples.Expander`: its containment check uses `String.startsWith` on the canonical target path without a separator/component-wise comparison, so an entry named like `../<target-dir-name>-sibling/file` writes outside the target directory whenever a sibling directory shares the target's canonical path as a string prefix. The repository's own pending 1.18 changelog describes exactly this "sibling directory / name is a prefix" edge case as having been fixed on 2018-06-15, yet the code in this snapshot still contains the unhardened prefix check, which is strong corroboration. I could not pinpoint a concrete defect for the other plausible lead (CVE-2018-11771-style infinite loop in ZipArchiveInputStream); that code contains multiple anti-loop guards, so it is recorded as a rejected lead rather than a candidate.
